content.text: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer anywhere in the document; § 12.3 expressly negates one.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier, preferred-supplier, or all-requirements obligation on Customer. § 12.3 affirmatively confirms that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling or using any product or service or engaging any supplier, and that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment; § 2.1 adds that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and that declining to place further Order Forms is not a breach. The only "exclusive" references elsewhere concern the non-exclusive licence to Customer (§ 13.1), exclusive-remedy/jurisdiction mechanics (§§ 19.4, 21, 28.2, 30) and § 12.4, which restricts Vendor from competing with Customer's analytics products — exclusivity running in Customer's favour, which the playbook treats as acceptable. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.
